// overrides: Advisory fixes for transitive packages nothing here depends on directly.
Each range stays INSIDE the major it patches: an override of '>=1.1.16'
also matches 5.0.8, so the loose form silently promoted every
brace-expansion in the tree onto the 5.x line. Caret ranges keep each
consumer on the major it was written against.
Drop an entry once the real dependency ships the fix itself.
A caret range does NOT keep itself current: '^1.1.16' happily resolves
1.1.17, so when the advisory moved to >=1.1.18 the pin was one patch short
and `pnpm audit` went back to failing. Three of these were in exactly that
state at once. When an advisory is re-published against a higher patch,
raise the floor here — the caret is what allows the fix, not what applies it.
nanoid is reached only through postcss, which runs at build time; the
advisory is a DoS in a custom-generator path this repo never calls. It is
pinned anyway because an advisory nobody can dismiss on sight is an
advisory that trains people to ignore the audit.
postcss and sharp are pinned by Next itself, so they need an override
rather than a bump: Next 15.5.22 depends on postcss 8.4.31 exactly and on
sharp ^0.34. Both are patch-compatible with the versions here. sharp is
only ever reached through the Image Optimizer, which this app has no
`images` config for and never calls — see next.config.mjs.
